source.title: A mean teacher algorithm for unlearning of language models

record.tranche_reason: The study tests recovery after unlearning by fine-tuning an unlearned model on unrelated alignment data, a different method from the attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own unlearning results on MUSE and a fine-tuning recovery experiment. The quantization and internal-representation recovery statements are cited from other work, not tested here, so they are not rows.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates its proposed mean-teacher unlearning algorithm with NLUL and KL/QKL regularization; it is not a reproduction of the original methods listed in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different outcomes across MUSE-News and MUSE-Books and between KL and QKL variants. The strongest MUSE-News knowledge-memorization reduction is paired with a substantial MMLU decrease.
record.problems: The recovery experiment reports no uncertainty and tests one unlearning configuration and one alignment dataset. The study does not state a chance level for knowmem f; its reference is the retrained model. The MUSE-Books target model already has degraded MMLU performance.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 results for additional AdamW baselines and other MUSE metrics were not included because they do not test the recovery attack; cited results from other papers were excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish that targeted accuracy is near chance; it reports MUSE knowledge-memorization scores and compares them with the retrain split. Its main recovery experiment is on one unlearned MUSE-News model.
It tests unrelated alignment-data fine-tuning, but not a few examples, loosely related examples, or a subset of forgotten facts.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of blocked access versus deletion is performed.
No prompt-only recovery attack is performed.
The study does not test a method for resisting the listed recovery attacks.
